F i g u r e 11.3 When an ionic solid (in this case, K2SO4) dissolves in wa- ter, the ions move away from their sites in the solid, where they were attracted strongly by ions of opposite electrical charge. New strong attractions replace those lost as each ion is surrounded by a group of water mol­e­cules. In a precipitation reaction, the process is reversed.
